items.title: A client with pneumonia is confused, has BP 84/48 mm Hg, HR 124/min, and lactate 4.2 mmol/L. Which action is the priority?
items.content: Activate the sepsis response and begin prescribed resuscitation and antimicrobial pathway.
items.rationale: Hypotension, altered mentation, and elevated lactate indicate impaired perfusion. Prompt protocol-based fluids and antimicrobials are time-critical.

items.title: A client reports chest pressure after using cocaine. BP is 190/108 mm Hg and HR 132/min. Which action should the nurse take first?
items.content: Obtain urgent ECG and initiate emergency assessment.
items.rationale: Cocaine can cause coronary vasospasm, ischemia, and dysrhythmias. Rapid ECG and assessment are needed; treatment is directed by emergency clinicians.

items.title: A client has abdominal distention, bilious vomiting, and high-pitched bowel sounds. Which prescription should the nurse anticipate?
items.content: Keep the client NPO and prepare for prescribed nasogastric decompression.
items.rationale: Findings suggest bowel obstruction. Bowel rest, fluid/electrolyte management, and decompression may be required while the cause is evaluated.

items.title: A client reports sudden severe eye pain, halos around lights, nausea, and a red eye. What is the priority?
items.content: Arrange immediate ophthalmologic evaluation.
items.rationale: Acute angle-closure glaucoma can rapidly cause permanent vision loss and is an emergency.

items.title: A client rescued from a house fire has facial burns, soot in the mouth, and hoarseness. Which action is the priority?
items.content: Activate emergency airway support and prepare for early airway management.
items.rationale: Hoarseness and soot suggest inhalation injury; airway edema can progress rapidly and make intubation difficult.

items.title: A client with acute pancreatitis develops perioral tingling and carpopedal spasm. Which laboratory result should the nurse review first?
items.content: Serum calcium.
items.rationale: Hypocalcemia can occur in severe pancreatitis and cause neuromuscular irritability, including tetany.

items.title: A client with atrial fibrillation develops sudden facial droop and unilateral weakness. What should the nurse do?
items.content: Activate the stroke response and establish last-known-well time.
items.rationale: Atrial fibrillation increases embolic stroke risk. Time-sensitive stroke evaluation must begin immediately.

items.title: A client with sickle cell disease reports severe generalized pain and has no respiratory symptoms. Which intervention is appropriate?
items.content: Administer prescribed analgesia promptly and assess hydration and oxygenation.
items.rationale: Pain crisis requires timely analgesia and assessment for complications. Oxygen is used for hypoxemia, not routinely when saturation is normal.

items.title: A hospitalized client with Parkinson disease is due for carbidopa-levodopa. The dose is delayed several hours. What should the nurse do?
items.content: Contact pharmacy and the prescriber to obtain the medication promptly.
items.rationale: Time-critical Parkinson medications should be administered on schedule when possible; delays can worsen rigidity, mobility, and swallowing.

items.title: A client with cirrhosis is increasingly confused and has asterixis. Which prescribed medication should the nurse anticipate?
items.content: Lactulose.
items.rationale: Lactulose reduces intestinal ammonia absorption and is commonly used for hepatic encephalopathy; monitor mental status and stool response.

items.title: A client taking metformin is scheduled for contrast-enhanced imaging and has reduced renal function. What should the nurse do?
items.content: Verify the current contrast and renal-function protocol with the prescriber before the study.
items.rationale: Metformin management around iodinated contrast depends on renal function and clinical circumstances; follow current institutional guidance and reassess renal function when indicated.

items.title: A client receiving gentamicin reports new ringing in both ears. What is the best action?
items.content: Hold the dose and notify the prescriber promptly.
items.rationale: Tinnitus may indicate ototoxicity. Prompt evaluation and drug-level/renal review can prevent progression.

items.title: A client receiving IV phenytoin develops hypotension and bradycardia during infusion. What should the nurse do?
items.content: Stop the infusion and initiate urgent assessment.
items.rationale: Rapid IV phenytoin administration can cause cardiovascular instability. Stop the infusion and escalate immediately.

items.title: A client has a new nitroglycerin patch prescribed daily. Which instruction is important?
items.content: Remove the previous patch before applying the new one and follow the prescribed nitrate-free interval.
items.rationale: Removing the old patch prevents unintended excess dosing; the prescribed nitrate-free interval helps reduce tolerance.

items.title: Two days after cesarean birth, a client has fever, uterine tenderness, and foul-smelling lochia. What should the nurse anticipate?
items.content: Prompt evaluation and prescribed broad-spectrum IV antibiotics.
items.rationale: Fever, uterine tenderness, and malodorous lochia suggest postpartum endometritis, requiring prompt antimicrobial treatment.

items.title: A newborn has grunting, nasal flaring, and intercostal retractions. What is the priority?
items.content: Support airway and breathing and notify the neonatal team immediately.
items.rationale: Grunting and retractions indicate respiratory distress. Rapid assessment and respiratory support are required.

items.title: An Rh-negative, unsensitized pregnant client delivers an Rh-positive newborn. Which intervention should the nurse anticipate?
items.content: Administer Rho(D) immune globulin within the recommended postpartum window.
items.rationale: Rho(D) immune globulin prevents maternal sensitization after exposure to Rh-positive fetal cells.

items.title: A 5-week-old has forceful nonbilious vomiting after feeds and remains hungry. Which finding is most likely?
items.content: A palpable olive-shaped mass in the upper abdomen.
items.rationale: Hypertrophic pyloric stenosis causes projectile nonbilious vomiting and may produce a palpable olive; dehydration and electrolyte abnormalities require evaluation.

items.title: A toddler with tetralogy of Fallot becomes cyanotic and dyspneic after crying. What should the nurse do first?
items.content: Place the child in the knee-chest position.
items.rationale: Knee-chest positioning increases systemic vascular resistance and can reduce right-to-left shunting during a hypercyanotic spell.

items.title: A child begins having a generalized tonic-clonic seizure in bed. What is the nurse's priority action?
items.content: Protect the child from injury and position laterally when possible.
items.rationale: Protecting the head and maintaining a safe position reduce injury and support airway drainage. Do not restrain or place objects in the mouth.

items.title: A client taking lithium has fever, vomiting, and poor oral intake. What should the nurse advise?
items.content: Seek prompt clinical advice and do not take further doses until urgently reviewed.
items.rationale: Dehydration can increase lithium concentration and toxicity risk. Prompt assessment of hydration, renal function, and serum level is needed.

items.title: A client says a voice is commanding them to harm a roommate. What should the nurse do first?
items.content: Assess intent, plan, ability to resist the command, and immediate access to means while maintaining safety.
items.rationale: Command hallucinations involving harm require immediate risk assessment, protection of others, and urgent team intervention.

items.title: During a sterile dressing change, the nurse's sterile glove touches the bedrail. What should the nurse do?
items.content: Replace the contaminated glove before continuing.
items.rationale: The bedrail is not sterile; contact contaminates the glove and compromises aseptic technique.

items.title: A postoperative client attempts to stand, falls, and reports hip pain. What should the nurse do first?
items.content: Assess the client for injury and neurologic or neurovascular compromise before moving them.
items.rationale: Do not move a potentially injured client until an assessment is completed and help is obtained.

items.title: A client with heart failure is preparing for discharge. Which instructions should the nurse include? Select all that apply.
items.content: Weigh daily under consistent conditions; report rapid weight gain according to the care plan; limit sodium as prescribed; take medications as directed; stop diuretics when edema resolves.
items.rationale: Daily weights detect fluid retention. Sodium guidance and medication adherence reduce exacerbations; diuretics should not be stopped without prescriber direction.

items.title: A client has severe neutropenia after chemotherapy. Which measures are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.content: Perform meticulous hand hygiene; avoid fresh flowers and standing water in the room; report fever immediately; screen visitors for illness.
items.rationale: Neutropenia increases infection risk. Fever requires urgent evaluation; reduce exposure to potential pathogens and use meticulous hygiene.

items.title: A client has dysphagia after stroke. Which findings should the nurse monitor during supervised oral intake? Select all that apply.
items.content: Coughing; wet or gurgling voice; pocketing food; oxygen desaturation.
items.rationale: These findings may indicate aspiration or impaired swallowing. Stop oral intake and request reassessment if they occur.

items.title: A client new to hemodialysis develops headache, nausea, restlessness, and confusion during treatment. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.content: Notify the dialysis clinician immediately; assess neurologic status and vital signs; prepare to modify or stop dialysis as prescribed.
items.rationale: Dialysis disequilibrium can cause cerebral edema and neurologic symptoms. Immediate assessment and treatment adjustment are required.

items.title: A client is prescribed an opioid for acute pain. Which teaching points are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.content: Avoid alcohol and sedatives unless specifically approved; do not drive while impaired; store securely; seek emergency help for slow or difficult breathing.
items.rationale: Opioids can cause sedation and respiratory depression. Secure storage reduces accidental ingestion or diversion.

items.title: Which instructions should the nurse include for a client taking warfarin? Select all that apply.
items.content: Keep vitamin K intake consistent; attend INR monitoring; report unusual bleeding; check with the prescriber before starting new medications or supplements.
items.rationale: Consistent vitamin K intake and INR monitoring support safe anticoagulation. Interactions and bleeding require prompt review.

items.title: A laboring client receiving oxytocin develops recurrent late decelerations. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.
items.content: Stop oxytocin; reposition laterally; increase IV fluid rate if prescribed or per protocol; notify the obstetric clinician and continue fetal assessment.
items.rationale: Late decelerations suggest uteroplacental insufficiency. Reduce uterine stimulation, reposition, support maternal circulation, and escalate.

items.title: Which newborn findings require prompt evaluation for pathologic jaundice? Select all that apply.
items.content: Jaundice within the first 24 hours; rapidly rising bilirubin; lethargy and poor feeding; signs of hemolysis.
items.rationale: Early onset, rapid bilirubin rise, poor feeding, and hemolysis increase risk of severe hyperbilirubinemia and bilirubin neurotoxicity.

items.title: Which interventions are appropriate for a child with cystic fibrosis? Select all that apply.
items.content: Give pancreatic enzymes with meals and snacks; encourage high-calorie nutrition; provide prescribed airway-clearance therapy; monitor growth and fat-soluble vitamin status.
items.rationale: Pancreatic insufficiency causes malabsorption. Enzymes with food, calorie-dense nutrition, airway clearance, and vitamin monitoring are standard components of care.

items.title: A child with nephrotic syndrome has generalized edema and heavy proteinuria. Which assessments are important? Select all that apply.
items.content: Daily weight; abdominal girth; urine protein; signs of infection; serum albumin and fluid balance.
items.rationale: Nephrotic syndrome causes protein loss, hypoalbuminemia, and edema, with increased infection and thrombosis risk.

items.title: A severely malnourished client begins nutritional rehabilitation. Which findings require close monitoring? Select all that apply.
items.content: Serum phosphate; potassium; magnesium; cardiac rhythm and fluid balance.
items.rationale: Refeeding syndrome can cause severe electrolyte shifts, dysrhythmias, fluid overload, and organ dysfunction. Monitor phosphate, potassium, magnesium, and cardiac status.

items.title: Which actions reduce central-line associated bloodstream infection risk? Select all that apply.
items.content: Scrub the hub before access; use aseptic technique; assess daily whether the line remains necessary; change dressings using sterile technique.
items.rationale: Hub disinfection, aseptic access, sterile dressing care, and daily necessity review reduce infection risk.

items.title: A postoperative client suddenly develops dyspnea and pleuritic pain. Select the 3 findings that support pulmonary embolism.
items.content: New tachycardia; unexplained hypoxemia; unilateral leg swelling.
items.rationale: Tachycardia and hypoxemia with unilateral leg swelling suggest venous thromboembolism with possible pulmonary embolism.

items.title: A client after thyroidectomy reports tingling around the mouth. Select the 3 findings consistent with hypocalcemia.
items.content: Positive Chvostek sign; carpopedal spasm; prolonged QT interval.
items.rationale: Hypocalcemia increases neuromuscular excitability and can prolong QT, creating risk for dysrhythmias.

items.title: A conscious client with diabetes has glucose 54 mg/dL and can swallow. Select the 3 appropriate actions.
items.content: Give 15 g of rapid-acting carbohydrate; recheck glucose in 15 minutes; repeat treatment if glucose remains below 70 mg/dL.
items.rationale: The 15-15 approach treats mild-to-moderate hypoglycemia in a conscious client able to swallow. Severe impairment requires glucagon or IV dextrose per protocol.

items.title: A postpartum client has fever, uterine tenderness, and tachycardia. Select the 3 priority nursing actions.
items.content: Notify the obstetric clinician; obtain ordered cultures without delaying antibiotics; monitor vital signs and perfusion.
items.rationale: These findings suggest postpartum infection with possible sepsis. Prompt escalation, cultures when feasible, antimicrobials, and perfusion monitoring are priorities.

items.title: A child with suspected bacterial meningitis is admitted. Select the 3 priority nursing actions.
items.content: Initiate appropriate isolation; perform frequent neurologic assessment; administer prescribed antimicrobials promptly.
items.rationale: Isolation limits transmission for relevant pathogens; neurologic assessment detects deterioration; early antimicrobials improve outcomes.

items.title: Which 3 activities must remain with the RN?
items.content: Initial assessment of a newly admitted unstable client; developing the nursing care plan; evaluating response to a new intervention.
items.rationale: Assessment, care planning, and evaluation require RN clinical judgment and cannot be delegated to UAP.

items.title: A client with pneumonia is tiring and becoming less responsive. Select the 3 signs of impending respiratory failure.
items.content: Declining level of consciousness; weak or ineffective cough; decreasing respiratory effort after prolonged distress.
items.rationale: Altered mentation, ineffective airway clearance, and fatigue with falling effort indicate impending respiratory failure.

items.title: Match each medication with the key monitoring parameter.
items.content: rows:unfractionated heparin;levothyroxine;furosemide|columns:aPTT or anti-Xa per protocol;TSH trend;potassium and renal function|answers:unfractionated heparin=aPTT or anti-Xa per protocol;levothyroxine=TSH trend;furosemide=potassium and renal function
items.rationale: Heparin is monitored using aPTT or anti-Xa protocols. Levothyroxine is titrated using thyroid function. Loop diuretics can affect potassium and renal function.

items.title: Match each laboratory pattern with the likely anemia type.
items.content: rows:low ferritin and low MCV;low vitamin B12 with macrocytosis;increased reticulocytes after acute blood loss|columns:iron deficiency;vitamin B12 deficiency;compensatory marrow response|answers:low ferritin and low MCV=iron deficiency;low vitamin B12 with macrocytosis=vitamin B12 deficiency;increased reticulocytes after acute blood loss=compensatory marrow response
items.rationale: Iron deficiency commonly causes microcytosis and low ferritin. B12 deficiency causes macrocytosis. Reticulocytosis reflects marrow response after blood loss.

items.title: For each finding, select all appropriate responses.
items.content: rows:weight gain of 2 kg in 2 days;new orthopnea;dizziness after diuretic dose|columns:contact care team promptly;assess blood pressure and volume status;do not independently double medication dose|answers:weight gain of 2 kg in 2 days=contact care team promptly;new orthopnea=contact care team promptly;dizziness after diuretic dose=assess blood pressure and volume status,contact care team promptly,do not independently double medication dose
items.rationale: Rapid weight gain and new orthopnea may signal worsening congestion. Dizziness may reflect hypotension or volume depletion and needs assessment; medication changes require clinical direction.

items.title: For each situation, select all appropriate actions.
items.content: rows:client using home oxygen;oxygen cylinder stored in room;nasal cannula tubing found kinked|columns:keep away from flames and smoking;secure cylinder upright;restore unobstructed tubing and reassess saturation|answers:client using home oxygen=keep away from flames and smoking;oxygen cylinder stored in room=secure cylinder upright;nasal cannula tubing found kinked=restore unobstructed tubing and reassess saturation
items.rationale: Oxygen supports combustion. Cylinders must be secured, and delivery tubing must remain unobstructed with reassessment of oxygenation.

items.title: A client with suspected stroke should remain ___ until swallowing safety is assessed. The nurse should document the ___ time and prepare for urgent ___ imaging.
items.content: NPO|last-known-well|noncontrast head CT
items.rationale: NPO status reduces aspiration risk. Last-known-well time guides treatment eligibility; noncontrast CT rapidly evaluates for intracranial hemorrhage.

items.title: Before giving digoxin, assess the ___ pulse for one full minute. If the client has new symptomatic bradycardia, ___ the dose and notify the ___.
items.content: apical|withhold|prescriber
items.rationale: Apical pulse assessment detects bradycardia. New symptomatic bradycardia warrants withholding and clinical review rather than automatic administration.

items.title: A client with a central line suddenly develops severe dyspnea, hypotension, absent breath sounds on the right, and tracheal deviation. Select the condition, two actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:tension pneumothorax|actions:activate emergency response and provide oxygen;prepare for immediate needle or finger decompression followed by chest tube as directed|monitor:oxygen saturation and respiratory effort;blood pressure and perfusion
items.rationale: Unilateral absent breath sounds, hypotension, and tracheal deviation suggest tension pneumothorax. This is a life-threatening emergency requiring immediate decompression.

items.title: During transfusion, a client develops fever, flank pain, hypotension, and dark urine. Select the condition, two actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:acute hemolytic transfusion reaction|actions:stop the transfusion and keep IV access with saline using new tubing;notify provider and blood bank and send ordered specimens|monitor:urine output and color;vital signs and hemolysis/renal laboratory trends
items.rationale: The symptoms suggest acute intravascular hemolysis. Stop the product, maintain access with saline, notify the team, and monitor for shock and acute kidney injury.

items.title: Highlight the findings that suggest worsening intracranial pressure in a client with meningitis: decreasing consciousness; repeated vomiting; new unequal pupils; improved headache; new seizure.
items.content: segments:decreasing consciousness|repeated vomiting|new unequal pupils|improved headache|new seizure|correct:1,2,3,5
items.rationale: Declining consciousness, vomiting, pupillary changes, and seizures may indicate neurologic deterioration or increased intracranial pressure and require immediate escalation.

items.title: Highlight the findings in a pregnant client with hypertension that indicate severe features: persistent severe headache; visual scotomata; BP 166/112 mm Hg; mild dependent ankle edema alone; right upper quadrant pain.
items.content: segments:persistent severe headache|visual scotomata|BP 166/112 mm Hg|mild dependent ankle edema alone|right upper quadrant pain|correct:1,2,3,5
items.rationale: Severe-range blood pressure, neurologic symptoms, and right upper quadrant pain are severe features and require urgent obstetric management.

items.title: The prescription is 375 mg. The liquid contains 250 mg per 5 mL. How many mL should the nurse administer?
items.rationale: 375 mg ÷ 250 mg × 5 mL = 7.5 mL. Verify the concentration and dose before administration.

items.title: A client drinks 240 mL juice, 180 mL water, and 120 mL soup. What is the total oral intake in mL?
items.rationale: 240 + 180 + 120 = 540 mL. Record intake according to facility measurement standards.

items.title: Arrange the usual sequence for removing PPE when wearing gloves, gown, eye protection, and mask.
items.content: Remove gloves.|Remove gown.|Perform hand hygiene if hands become contaminated.|Remove eye protection.|Remove mask or respirator after leaving the room when indicated.|Perform hand hygiene.
items.rationale: Remove the most contaminated items first and avoid touching the face. Respirator removal follows isolation-room exit requirements; hand hygiene is performed at key points.

items.title: Arrange the response for a conscious client with glucose 58 mg/dL who can swallow.
items.content: Give 15 g of rapid-acting carbohydrate.|Recheck blood glucose in 15 minutes.|Repeat 15 g carbohydrate if glucose remains below 70 mg/dL.|Once corrected, provide a meal or snack if the next meal is not soon.
items.rationale: Treat promptly with fast carbohydrate, recheck after 15 minutes, repeat if still low, and prevent recurrence with food when appropriate.

items.title: A client with COPD is preparing for discharge. Select all appropriate teaching points.
items.content: Use prescribed inhalers with correct technique; receive recommended vaccinations; stop smoking and seek cessation support; pace activity and plan rest periods; increase oxygen flow independently whenever dyspneic.
items.rationale: Correct inhaler use, vaccination, smoking cessation, and pacing reduce exacerbations and symptoms. Oxygen changes should follow the prescribed plan.

items.title: A client is prescribed apixaban. Select all appropriate teaching points.
items.content: Take doses consistently as prescribed; report unusual bleeding; inform clinicians before procedures; do not double a missed dose without following product instructions; avoid all vegetables containing vitamin K.
items.rationale: Apixaban has no routine vitamin K dietary restriction. Adherence, bleeding surveillance, and procedural communication are important; missed-dose instructions should follow product guidance.

items.title: A client with suspected sepsis has lactate 4.8 mmol/L and MAP 58 mm Hg. After prescribed fluids, MAP is 66 mm Hg and lactate is 3.1 mmol/L. What does this trend indicate?
items.content: Perfusion is improving but remains abnormal; continue close reassessment and prescribed sepsis management.
items.rationale: Improved MAP and falling lactate suggest response to resuscitation, but continued monitoring and treatment are needed until perfusion stabilizes.

items.title: A client with head injury has GCS scores of 15, 13, and 10 over three assessments and develops a new episode of vomiting. What is the priority?
items.content: Recognize neurologic deterioration and activate urgent escalation for possible intracranial injury progression.
items.rationale: A declining GCS with vomiting indicates worsening neurologic status and possible increased intracranial pressure. Immediate escalation is required.

items.title: A 68-year-old with COPD presents with increased sputum, wheezing, and dyspnea. RR 30/min, SpO₂ 84% on room air, accessory muscle use, and ABG pH 7.29, PaCO₂ 62 mm Hg. What is the priority problem and nursing plan?
items.content: Acute COPD exacerbation with hypoxemia and hypercapnic respiratory acidosis. Titrate prescribed oxygen to the individualized target, administer prescribed bronchodilators and corticosteroids, monitor mental status and ABGs, and escalate for noninvasive ventilation or airway support if deterioration continues.
items.rationale: The client has acute ventilatory failure with respiratory acidosis. Controlled oxygen, bronchodilation, steroids, and close reassessment are indicated; worsening fatigue or mentation requires escalation.

items.title: A client 3 days postpartum reports severe headache and blurred vision. BP is 172/114 mm Hg. The client has brisk reflexes and epigastric discomfort. What complication is suspected and what are the priorities?
items.content: Suspect postpartum preeclampsia with severe features. Notify the obstetric team urgently, institute seizure precautions, administer prescribed magnesium sulfate and antihypertensive therapy, and monitor respiratory status, reflexes, urine output, and blood pressure.
items.rationale: Preeclampsia can first present or worsen postpartum. Severe hypertension and neurologic symptoms create seizure and stroke risk; magnesium and rapid blood pressure control are urgent.

items.title: A 59-year-old with a history of peptic ulcer disease reports black stools and dizziness. BP 88/54 mm Hg, HR 122/min, cool skin, and hemoglobin 7.4 g/dL. What is the priority nursing response?
items.content: Suspect significant gastrointestinal hemorrhage with hypovolemia. Activate urgent clinical support, establish large-bore IV access, prepare prescribed fluid and blood-product resuscitation, keep NPO, and monitor hemodynamics and ongoing bleeding.
items.rationale: Melena, hypotension, tachycardia, and anemia indicate significant blood loss. Stabilization and urgent evaluation take priority.

items.title: A client taking methimazole reports fever and sore throat. What should the nurse advise?
items.content: Withhold further doses pending urgent evaluation and obtain a CBC as prescribed.
items.rationale: Fever and sore throat may indicate agranulocytosis, a rare serious adverse effect. Prompt blood count and prescriber review are needed.

items.title: Which teaching should the nurse provide to a client with peripheral arterial disease? Select all that apply.
items.content: Stop smoking; inspect feet daily; avoid direct heating pads on feet; follow a structured walking program if prescribed; avoid crossing legs for prolonged periods.
items.rationale: Smoking cessation, foot protection, and exercise therapy support limb health. Reduced sensation and perfusion increase burn and injury risk.

items.title: A client with pancreatitis develops systemic deterioration. Select the 3 findings that require urgent escalation.
items.content: New hypotension; oxygen saturation falling despite oxygen; reduced level of consciousness.
items.rationale: These findings suggest shock, respiratory failure, or systemic complications and require immediate escalation.

items.title: Match each burn description with the likely depth.
items.content: rows:red, painful, dry skin without blisters;moist blistered skin with severe pain;white or charred leathery skin with reduced sensation|columns:superficial;superficial partial-thickness;full-thickness|answers:red, painful, dry skin without blisters=superficial;moist blistered skin with severe pain=superficial partial-thickness;white or charred leathery skin with reduced sensation=full-thickness
items.rationale: Superficial burns are red and dry. Superficial partial-thickness burns are moist, blistered, and painful. Full-thickness burns may be leathery and insensate centrally.

items.title: A client with sudden dyspnea, pleuritic pain, and hypoxemia may have a ___. The nurse should activate urgent assessment, support ___, and avoid unnecessary ___.
items.content: pulmonary embolism|oxygenation|ambulation
items.rationale: Pulmonary embolism can cause acute respiratory and hemodynamic compromise. Support oxygenation, escalate, and keep the client at rest during evaluation.

items.title: A client arrives with sudden aphasia and unilateral weakness, last known well 45 minutes ago. Select the condition, two actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:acute stroke, possible ischemic|actions:activate stroke pathway and document last-known-well;prepare for urgent noncontrast CT and glucose assessment|monitor:neurologic status;blood pressure and oxygenation
items.rationale: Rapid stroke activation, onset documentation, and CT are essential. Serial neurologic checks and physiologic monitoring identify deterioration and support treatment decisions.

items.title: Highlight the actions that reduce medication error risk: verify two client identifiers; prepare medications for several clients together without separation; check allergies; clarify an incomplete order; document before administration.
items.content: segments:verify two client identifiers|prepare medications for several clients together without separation|check allergies|clarify an incomplete order|document before administration|correct:1,3,4
items.rationale: Use two identifiers, check allergies, clarify incomplete orders, and document after administration. Preparing medications for multiple clients together increases mix-up risk.

items.title: A medication is prescribed at 5 mg/kg. The client weighs 60 kg. What is the total dose in mg?
items.rationale: 5 mg/kg × 60 kg = 300 mg. Confirm the dose range and formulation before preparation.

items.title: A client's creatinine increases from 0.8 to 1.1 to 1.9 mg/dL over 48 hours, while urine output falls to 0.4 mL/kg/hr. What is the priority interpretation?
items.content: The client has worsening acute kidney injury and requires prompt evaluation of perfusion, volume status, medications, and electrolytes.
items.rationale: A rapid creatinine rise with reduced urine output indicates acute kidney injury. Assess reversible causes and complications promptly.

items.title: A confused client repeatedly attempts to climb out of bed. Which intervention should the nurse try first?
items.content: Use individualized alternatives such as frequent observation, toileting, reorientation, and a low bed.
items.rationale: Restraints are a last resort. Address unmet needs and use the least restrictive safe alternatives.

items.title: Which instructions are appropriate for a client using insulin at home? Select all that apply.
items.content: Follow product-specific storage instructions; inspect insulin for unexpected particles or discoloration; rotate injection sites; avoid sharing pens or needles.
items.rationale: Insulin stability varies by product. Visual inspection, site rotation, and never sharing injection devices reduce risk.

items.title: A newborn is lethargic, feeds poorly, has temperature instability, and develops apnea. Select the 3 priority actions.
items.content: Notify neonatal clinician immediately; support airway and breathing; obtain ordered cultures and administer prescribed antimicrobials promptly.
items.rationale: Neonatal sepsis can present nonspecifically and progress rapidly. Respiratory support and prompt evaluation/treatment are essential.

items.title: For each medication, select all safety checks that apply.
items.content: rows:IV insulin;heparin infusion;concentrated potassium chloride|columns:independent double-check per policy;use infusion pump and protocol;never administer by IV push|answers:IV insulin=independent double-check per policy,use infusion pump and protocol;heparin infusion=independent double-check per policy,use infusion pump and protocol;concentrated potassium chloride=independent double-check per policy,use infusion pump and protocol,never administer by IV push
items.rationale: Insulin and heparin are high-alert medications requiring protocolized administration and checks. Concentrated potassium must be diluted and infused under policy; never give IV push.

items.title: Arrange the immediate response when a client receiving magnesium sulfate has RR 8/min and absent reflexes.
items.content: Stop the magnesium sulfate infusion.|Call for emergency assistance and notify the obstetric clinician.|Support airway and breathing and monitor oxygenation.|Prepare and administer prescribed calcium gluconate.
items.rationale: Respiratory depression and absent reflexes indicate magnesium toxicity. Stop the infusion, escalate, support ventilation, and use calcium gluconate as prescribed.

items.title: A client with acute kidney injury is oliguric. Select all appropriate nursing actions.
items.content: Measure intake and output accurately; trend creatinine, potassium, and bicarbonate; assess lung sounds and edema; review nephrotoxic exposures; administer potassium supplements without checking the level.
items.rationale: Monitor renal function, electrolytes, and fluid overload, and review nephrotoxins. Potassium replacement without a current level is unsafe in oliguria.

items.title: A 64-year-old with end-stage kidney disease missed dialysis. The client reports weakness and palpitations. Potassium is 7.0 mEq/L; ECG shows widened QRS complexes. What is the priority response?
items.content: Treat as life-threatening hyperkalemia: activate emergency support, prepare IV calcium for membrane stabilization, administer prescribed potassium-shifting therapy, and arrange urgent dialysis. Continuously monitor ECG and repeat potassium.
items.rationale: Severe hyperkalemia with ECG changes can cause fatal dysrhythmias. Calcium stabilizes the myocardium, shifting therapies temporarily lower serum potassium, and dialysis removes potassium.

items.title: A 20-month-old has a brief generalized seizure with fever and returns to baseline. Which teaching is appropriate?
items.content: Place the child on the side during a seizure and seek emergency help if it lasts 5 minutes or breathing is impaired.
items.rationale: Most simple febrile seizures are brief and self-limited. Protect the child, time the seizure, and seek emergency care for prolonged seizure or breathing compromise.

items.title: A client taking clozapine reports fever and sore throat. What should the nurse do?
items.content: Arrange urgent assessment and ANC testing before further dosing.
items.rationale: Clozapine can cause severe neutropenia. Infection symptoms require urgent ANC evaluation and prescriber direction.

items.title: A client with suspected appendicitis reports sudden relief of severe right lower quadrant pain followed by generalized abdominal pain and fever. What should the nurse suspect?
items.content: Appendiceal perforation with peritonitis.
items.rationale: Sudden pain relief followed by diffuse pain and fever may indicate rupture and peritoneal contamination; urgent surgical evaluation is required.

items.title: Which interventions reduce venous thromboembolism risk in an immobile postoperative client? Select all that apply.
items.content: Assist with early ambulation when safe; apply prescribed intermittent pneumatic compression; administer prescribed prophylactic anticoagulant; encourage leg exercises.
items.rationale: Mobility, mechanical prophylaxis, and prescribed anticoagulation reduce venous stasis and thrombosis risk.

items.title: Select the 3 descriptions consistent with a stage 2 pressure injury.
items.content: Partial-thickness skin loss with exposed dermis; a moist pink or red wound bed; an intact or ruptured serum-filled blister.
items.rationale: Stage 2 involves partial-thickness skin loss and exposed dermis, often appearing as a moist pink/red wound or serum blister.

items.title: Match each ABG with the primary disorder.
items.content: rows:pH 7.28 PaCO2 58 HCO3 25;pH 7.50 PaCO2 40 HCO3 31;pH 7.30 PaCO2 38 HCO3 18|columns:respiratory acidosis;metabolic alkalosis;metabolic acidosis|answers:pH 7.28 PaCO2 58 HCO3 25=respiratory acidosis;pH 7.50 PaCO2 40 HCO3 31=metabolic alkalosis;pH 7.30 PaCO2 38 HCO3 18=metabolic acidosis
items.rationale: Low pH with elevated PaCO2 indicates respiratory acidosis. High pH with elevated bicarbonate indicates metabolic alkalosis. Low pH with low bicarbonate indicates metabolic acidosis.

items.title: After a long-bone fracture, worsening pain with passive stretch and tense swelling suggest ___. The nurse should keep the limb at ___ heart level and urgently notify the ___.
items.content: compartment syndrome|approximately|orthopedic team
items.rationale: These findings suggest compartment syndrome. Avoid elevation above heart level or ice that could reduce perfusion; urgent surgical evaluation is required.

items.title: A client with Addison disease has vomiting, hypotension, weakness, sodium 124 mEq/L, and potassium 6.1 mEq/L. Select the condition, two actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:adrenal crisis|actions:administer prescribed IV hydrocortisone;initiate prescribed isotonic fluid resuscitation|monitor:blood pressure and perfusion;serum glucose and electrolytes
items.rationale: Adrenal crisis causes severe cortisol deficiency, volume depletion, and electrolyte disturbance. Steroid replacement and fluids are urgent; monitor hemodynamics, glucose, and electrolytes.

items.title: Highlight the classic findings of acute limb ischemia: sudden severe limb pain; pallor; pulselessness; paresthesia; chronic mild ankle edema.
items.content: segments:sudden severe limb pain|pallor|pulselessness|paresthesia|chronic mild ankle edema|correct:1,2,3,4
items.rationale: The 6 Ps include pain, pallor, pulselessness, paresthesia, paralysis, and poikilothermia. Acute limb ischemia is a vascular emergency.

items.title: A client’s temperature is 39.0 °C. Convert to Fahrenheit using F = (C × 9/5) + 32. Enter to one decimal place.
After surgery, a client's HR rises from 84 to 118/min, BP falls from 122/76 to 90/54 mm Hg, and urine output decreases from 45 to 15 mL/hr. What should the nurse suspect?
items.content: Ongoing blood loss or shock with impaired organ perfusion; escalate immediately.
items.rationale: Tachycardia, hypotension, and oliguria are signs of worsening perfusion and possible hemorrhage.

items.title: A client taking propranolol daily says they stopped it abruptly yesterday. Which risk should the nurse explain?
items.content: Rebound tachycardia, hypertension, or angina can occur; contact the prescriber for guidance.
items.rationale: Abrupt beta-blocker withdrawal can cause rebound sympathetic effects and exacerbate ischemia. Tapering is generally clinician-directed.

items.title: Which instructions support bone health for an older adult with osteoporosis? Select all that apply.
items.content: Perform weight-bearing activity as tolerated; ensure adequate calcium and vitamin D intake; remove home fall hazards; stop smoking.
items.rationale: Weight-bearing exercise, adequate nutrients, fall prevention, and smoking cessation support bone health and reduce fracture risk.

items.title: Select the 3 findings that can indicate increased intracranial pressure.
items.content: Declining level of consciousness; new pupillary asymmetry; abnormal posturing.
items.rationale: These are concerning neurologic signs of rising intracranial pressure and require urgent escalation.

items.title: For each practice, select whether it supports safe sleep.
items.content: rows:place infant supine;use a firm flat sleep surface;place pillows and loose blankets in crib;room-share without bed-sharing|columns:recommended;not recommended|answers:place infant supine=recommended;use a firm flat sleep surface=recommended;place pillows and loose blankets in crib=not recommended;room-share without bed-sharing=recommended
items.rationale: Supine positioning, a firm flat surface, and room-sharing without bed-sharing reduce sleep-related infant death risk. Keep soft objects and loose bedding out of the sleep space.

items.title: Arrange the initial actions for a client with anaphylaxis and hypotension.
items.content: Administer IM epinephrine promptly per protocol.|Call for emergency assistance and support airway and breathing.|Position supine with legs elevated if tolerated and no respiratory compromise.|Administer prescribed oxygen and IV fluids; reassess frequently.
items.rationale: Epinephrine is first-line and should not be delayed. Support airway, breathing, and circulation; position based on respiratory status and reassess.

items.title: Select all appropriate interventions for a postoperative client at risk for atelectasis.
items.content: Encourage incentive spirometry as instructed; assist with early mobilization; teach splinting during cough; reposition regularly; maintain prolonged strict bed rest.
items.rationale: Lung expansion, coughing, repositioning, and mobility reduce atelectasis. Prolonged bed rest increases pulmonary complications.

items.title: A 58-year-old reports 40 minutes of chest pressure radiating to the jaw with diaphoresis. ECG shows ST elevation in contiguous leads. BP 146/88 mm Hg, HR 104/min, SpO₂ 95%. What is the priority plan?
items.content: Activate the STEMI pathway, obtain IV access and required labs without delaying reperfusion, administer prescribed antiplatelet therapy after contraindication review, and prepare for urgent reperfusion. Monitor rhythm, pain, and hemodynamic status.
items.rationale: ST elevation with typical ischemic symptoms indicates STEMI. Rapid reperfusion is the priority; tests and medications must not delay definitive treatment.

items.title: A postoperative client has suprapubic discomfort and has not voided for 8 hours. Bladder scan shows 780 mL. What should the nurse do?
items.content: Notify the prescriber and perform catheterization if prescribed or authorized by protocol.
items.rationale: The large residual indicates urinary retention. Prompt bladder decompression may be required while reversible causes are assessed.

items.title: A client develops wheezing, facial swelling, and hypotension after an antibiotic dose. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.content: Stop the medication; administer IM epinephrine per emergency protocol; activate emergency response; support airway and oxygenation.
items.rationale: These are signs of anaphylaxis. Stop exposure, give epinephrine promptly, and support airway and circulation.

items.title: Select the 3 findings that suggest worsening oxygenation in an adult with pneumonia.
items.content: New confusion; central cyanosis; increasing work of breathing with falling saturation.
items.rationale: Altered mentation, cyanosis, and increased respiratory effort with hypoxemia indicate deterioration.

items.title: Match each infection with the primary transmission-based precaution.
items.content: rows:measles;influenza;MRSA wound with uncontrolled drainage|columns:airborne;droplet;contact|answers:measles=airborne;influenza=droplet;MRSA wound with uncontrolled drainage=contact
items.rationale: Measles requires airborne precautions, influenza droplet precautions, and uncontrolled draining MRSA wounds contact precautions.

items.title: A client receiving unfractionated heparin develops serious bleeding. The nurse should stop the infusion and anticipate prescribed ___ as a reversal agent while monitoring ___ and hemodynamic status.
items.content: protamine sulfate|aPTT
items.rationale: Protamine reverses unfractionated heparin. Monitor coagulation parameters and clinical bleeding response.

items.title: A client with heart failure suddenly becomes severely dyspneic, has crackles, pink frothy sputum, and SpO₂ 80%. Select the condition, two actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:acute pulmonary edema|actions:activate emergency response and support oxygenation;position upright and prepare prescribed ventilatory and diuretic therapy|monitor:oxygen saturation and respiratory effort;blood pressure and urine output
items.rationale: Severe pulmonary congestion with hypoxemia is life-threatening. Escalate, support ventilation, position upright, and prepare prescribed therapy while monitoring response.

items.title: Highlight the actions that reduce aspiration risk after stroke: complete swallow screening before oral intake; offer thin water before assessment; position upright for meals; check for food pocketing; keep suction available when indicated.
items.content: segments:complete swallow screening before oral intake|offer thin water before assessment|position upright for meals|check for food pocketing|keep suction available when indicated|correct:1,3,4,5
items.rationale: Swallow screening before intake, upright positioning, checking for pocketing, and appropriate suction readiness reduce aspiration harm.

items.title: A client’s weight increases from 68.2 kg to 70.0 kg. What is the weight gain in kg?
items.rationale: 70.0 − 68.2 = 1.8 kg. Rapid weight gain may reflect fluid retention and should be interpreted with the care plan.

items.title: A client taking lithium has a level of 0.8 mEq/L last week and 1.7 mEq/L today with vomiting and coarse tremor. What is the priority?
items.content: Suspect lithium toxicity; withhold further doses pending urgent prescriber direction and obtain clinical assessment.
items.rationale: A rising level above the usual therapeutic range with toxicity symptoms requires urgent evaluation, hydration assessment, and renal/electrolyte review.

items.title: A client with a high spinal cord injury develops hypotension, bradycardia, and warm dry skin. Which complication should the nurse suspect?
items.content: Neurogenic shock.
items.rationale: Loss of sympathetic tone can cause hypotension, bradycardia, and vasodilation after spinal cord injury.

items.title: A client with pancreatic cancer has jaundice, pruritus, and pale stools. Which nursing actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.content: Assess skin integrity; monitor bilirubin and liver tests; provide prescribed antipruritic care; assess nutritional status and stool changes.
items.rationale: Biliary obstruction can cause cholestasis, pruritus, pale stools, and malabsorption. Monitor hepatic function, skin, and nutrition.

items.title: Select the 3 actions appropriate for recurrent late decelerations during oxytocin infusion.
items.content: Stop oxytocin; reposition the client laterally; notify the obstetric clinician promptly.
items.rationale: These actions reduce uterine stimulation, may improve perfusion, and escalate evaluation of fetal compromise.

items.title: For each abnormality, select the appropriate safety focus.
items.content: rows:potassium 2.8 mEq/L;magnesium 1.1 mg/dL;sodium 119 mEq/L|columns:monitor cardiac rhythm;assess neuromuscular irritability;monitor neurologic status and correction rate|answers:potassium 2.8 mEq/L=monitor cardiac rhythm;magnesium 1.1 mg/dL=assess neuromuscular irritability,monitor cardiac rhythm;sodium 119 mEq/L=monitor neurologic status and correction rate
items.rationale: Hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia can cause dysrhythmias. Hypomagnesemia also causes neuromuscular irritability. Severe hyponatremia requires neurologic monitoring and careful correction.

items.title: An 8-year-old with asthma has severe wheezing, speaks in one-word phrases, RR 36/min, and SpO₂ 89%. After initial bronchodilator, breath sounds become very faint and the child is drowsy. What is the priority?
items.content: Recognize impending respiratory failure, activate emergency airway support, provide oxygen and prescribed rescue therapy, and prepare for ventilatory support.
items.rationale: A quiet chest with drowsiness after severe distress suggests critically reduced airflow and fatigue, not improvement. Immediate escalation is essential.

items.title: A client experiencing paranoid delusions refuses food because they believe it is poisoned. Which response is most therapeutic?
items.content: Offer sealed, unopened food and acknowledge the client's fear without reinforcing the delusion.
items.rationale: A practical choice can support nutrition and trust. Validate emotion without agreeing with the delusional belief.

items.title: Which interventions may reduce delirium in an older hospitalized client? Select all that apply.
items.content: Provide orientation cues; promote sleep hygiene; ensure sensory aids are available; encourage mobility and hydration; minimize unnecessary room changes.
items.rationale: Orientation, sleep, sensory support, mobility, and hydration reduce delirium risk. Investigate acute causes such as infection, medication effects, and hypoxia.

items.title: Select the 3 immediate nursing priorities for suspected compartment syndrome.
items.content: Notify the surgical team urgently; perform and document neurovascular assessments; prepare for pressure-relieving intervention as prescribed.
items.rationale: Compartment syndrome threatens limb viability. Urgent surgical evaluation and serial neurovascular assessment are essential.

items.title: Match each insulin with its general action profile.
items.content: rows:lispro;regular;glargine|columns:rapid acting;short acting;long acting basal|answers:lispro=rapid acting;regular=short acting;glargine=long acting basal
items.rationale: Lispro is rapid acting, regular insulin is short acting, and glargine provides long-acting basal coverage. Timing must follow product guidance and meal availability.

items.title: A client with aortic stenosis reports exertional syncope and chest pain. These symptoms suggest reduced ___ output. The nurse should avoid unmonitored strenuous ___ and report symptoms promptly to the ___.
items.content: cardiac|activity|cardiology team
items.rationale: Aortic stenosis obstructs left ventricular outflow. Syncope and angina suggest limited cardiac output and require prompt specialist assessment.

items.title: A client with diabetes is unconscious, glucose 32 mg/dL, and has no IV access. Select the condition, two actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:severe hypoglycemia|actions:administer prescribed glucagon by an available approved route;activate emergency response and establish IV access for dextrose if needed|monitor:repeat blood glucose;level of consciousness and ability to swallow safely
items.rationale: Unconscious hypoglycemia is an emergency. Give glucagon if IV access is unavailable, obtain emergency support, and reassess glucose and neurologic status.

items.title: Highlight findings indicating worsening fluid overload: increasing orthopnea; new crackles; rapid weight gain; reduced peripheral edema; rising jugular venous pressure.
items.content: segments:increasing orthopnea|new crackles|rapid weight gain|reduced peripheral edema|rising jugular venous pressure|correct:1,2,3,5
items.rationale: Orthopnea, crackles, rapid weight gain, and elevated JVP indicate worsening congestion. Reduced edema alone does not suggest fluid overload.

items.title: A client is prescribed 0.5 mg of a medication. Tablets are 0.25 mg each. How many tablets should be given?
items.content: 2|tablets|0
items.rationale: 0.5 mg ÷ 0.25 mg/tablet = 2 tablets. Verify the prescribed dose and tablet formulation.

items.title: A client with suspected shock has MAP readings of 62, 58, and 54 mm Hg with decreasing urine output. What is the priority interpretation?
items.content: Perfusion is worsening and requires immediate escalation and prescribed hemodynamic support.
items.rationale: A falling MAP with oliguria indicates worsening organ perfusion. Prompt escalation and reassessment are necessary.

items.title: A 76-year-old admitted with ischemic stroke has facial weakness and slurred speech. During a bedside water trial, the client coughs and develops a wet voice. What should the nurse do?
items.content: Stop the oral trial, maintain NPO status, notify the clinician, and request formal swallowing evaluation. Continue aspiration precautions and provide oral care.
items.rationale: Coughing and wet voice indicate possible aspiration. Oral intake should stop pending formal swallowing assessment; oral hygiene reduces aspiration pneumonia risk.

items.title: Immediately after placental delivery, a client has severe hemorrhage, shock, and a mass protruding from the vagina; the uterine fundus is not palpable abdominally. What should the nurse suspect?
items.content: Uterine inversion and activate the obstetric emergency response.
items.rationale: A missing abdominal fundus with a vaginal mass and hemorrhage suggests uterine inversion, a life-threatening obstetric emergency.

items.title: Which interventions are appropriate for a client with increased intracranial pressure? Select all that apply.
items.content: Elevate the head of bed as prescribed; keep head and neck midline; avoid unnecessary stimulation; prevent hypoxia and hypotension; cluster all care into prolonged sessions.
items.rationale: Positioning and prevention of hypoxia/hypotension support cerebral perfusion. Avoid excessive stimulation and prolonged clustering that can increase ICP.

items.title: Select the 3 priority elements of medication reconciliation at admission.
items.content: Compare the client's actual medication use with the current orders; verify allergies and prior adverse reactions; identify duplicate therapies and high-risk interactions.
items.rationale: Accurate reconciliation requires a best possible medication history, allergy review, and identification of discrepancies, duplication, and interactions.

items.title: Match each clinical pattern with the likely shock category.
items.content: rows:severe dehydration with tachycardia and flat neck veins;sepsis with warm flushed skin early and hypotension;massive MI with pulmonary crackles and hypotension|columns:hypovolemic;distributive;cardiogenic|answers:severe dehydration with tachycardia and flat neck veins=hypovolemic;sepsis with warm flushed skin early and hypotension=distributive;massive MI with pulmonary crackles and hypotension=cardiogenic
items.rationale: Volume loss causes hypovolemic shock; sepsis causes distributive shock; pump failure with pulmonary congestion suggests cardiogenic shock.

items.title: A client with unilateral calf swelling and pain after surgery may have a ___. The nurse should avoid massaging the limb and anticipate diagnostic ___ as prescribed.
items.content: deep vein thrombosis|ultrasound
items.rationale: Unilateral swelling and pain suggest DVT. Massage is avoided; duplex ultrasound is commonly used for diagnosis.

items.title: A client with Graves disease has fever 40.2 °C, HR 160/min, agitation, and diarrhea. Select the condition, two actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:thyroid storm|actions:activate urgent medical response and initiate cooling measures;administer prescribed beta blocker and antithyroid therapy|monitor:heart rate and rhythm;temperature and mental status
items.rationale: Thyroid storm is a life-threatening hypermetabolic emergency. Cooling, beta blockade, and antithyroid therapy are used with close cardiovascular and neurologic monitoring.

items.title: Highlight findings of severe dehydration in an infant: lethargy; markedly delayed capillary refill; absent tears; normal wet diapers; weak peripheral pulses.
items.content: segments:lethargy|markedly delayed capillary refill|absent tears|normal wet diapers|weak peripheral pulses|correct:1,2,3,5
items.rationale: Lethargy, delayed refill, absent tears, and weak pulses indicate significant volume depletion and impaired perfusion.

items.title: A 70-kg adult produces 21 mL of urine in 1 hour. Calculate urine output in mL/kg/hr to two decimal places.
items.rationale: 21 mL ÷ 70 kg = 0.30 mL/kg/hr, below the usual adult target of at least 0.5 mL/kg/hr.

items.title: A chemotherapy client's temperature rises from 37.2 °C to 38.1 °C and ANC is 400/mm³. What is the priority?
items.content: Treat as febrile neutropenia and activate urgent evaluation and antimicrobial pathway.
items.rationale: Fever with severe neutropenia is an emergency even without localizing symptoms; prompt empiric antimicrobial treatment is required.

items.title: A 63-year-old on postoperative day 2 develops sudden dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, HR 132/min, BP 94/58 mm Hg, and SpO₂ 85%. One calf is swollen. What is the priority nursing plan?
items.content: Suspect pulmonary embolism with possible hemodynamic compromise. Activate rapid response, support oxygenation, keep the client at rest, establish monitoring and IV access, and prepare for urgent imaging and prescribed anticoagulation or advanced therapy.
items.rationale: Sudden respiratory symptoms, hypoxemia, tachycardia, hypotension, and unilateral leg swelling suggest PE. Immediate stabilization and urgent evaluation are necessary.

items.title: A competent adult client refuses a prescribed medication after receiving an explanation. What should the nurse do?
items.content: Respect the refusal, assess the reason, provide relevant information, and notify the prescriber as appropriate.
items.rationale: Competent adults may refuse treatment. The nurse should explore concerns, educate without coercion, document, and communicate the decision.

items.title: Which findings should a client with a new ileostomy report promptly? Select all that apply.
items.content: Stoma becomes dusky or black; persistent absence of output with cramping and vomiting; signs of dehydration; markedly increased watery output.
items.rationale: Dusky/black stoma may indicate ischemia. Obstruction and high-output ileostomy can cause dehydration and electrolyte loss.

items.title: Select the 3 postpartum symptoms that require urgent evaluation.
items.content: Heavy bleeding soaking a pad in an hour or less; severe headache with visual changes; chest pain or difficulty breathing.
items.rationale: These may indicate hemorrhage, postpartum preeclampsia, pulmonary embolism, or cardiac complications and require urgent care.

items.title: For each specimen, select the appropriate collection principle.
items.content: rows:clean-catch urine;blood culture;stool for occult blood|columns:cleanse and collect midstream;use aseptic venipuncture and collect before antibiotics when feasible;avoid contamination with urine or toilet water|answers:clean-catch urine=cleanse and collect midstream;blood culture=use aseptic venipuncture and collect before antibiotics when feasible;stool for occult blood=avoid contamination with urine or toilet water
items.rationale: Correct collection reduces contamination and false results. Blood cultures should be obtained before antibiotics when feasible without delaying urgent treatment.

items.title: Arrange the initial actions for a client with active hematemesis and hypotension.
items.content: Activate emergency response and assess airway, breathing, and circulation.|Position to protect airway and provide oxygen as indicated.|Establish large-bore IV access and initiate prescribed resuscitation.|Prepare for ordered blood products and urgent endoscopic evaluation.
items.rationale: Stabilization begins with ABCs and escalation, followed by IV access and resuscitation. Definitive evaluation follows stabilization.

items.title: Select all appropriate teaching points for a client with advanced chronic kidney disease.
items.content: Follow individualized sodium, potassium, phosphorus, and fluid guidance; attend scheduled renal appointments; report reduced urine output or new dyspnea; avoid OTC NSAIDs unless approved; use salt substitutes freely.
items.rationale: Diet and fluid limits must be individualized. NSAIDs can worsen renal function; many salt substitutes contain potassium and may be unsafe.

items.title: A client admitted for depression says, “I have saved enough medication to end my life when I get home.” The client has a prior attempt and refuses to discuss a safety plan. What is the priority?
items.content: Treat as high and potentially imminent suicide risk: maintain continuous observation per policy, secure medications and other means, notify the psychiatric team urgently, and complete direct risk assessment and safety planning.
items.rationale: A specific plan, access to means, prior attempt, and refusal of safety planning indicate high risk. Protect the client and escalate immediately; do not leave the client alone.

items.title: A client with a known severe food allergy develops throat tightness and wheezing after accidental exposure. Which action should the client take?
items.content: Use the epinephrine autoinjector immediately and activate emergency medical services.
items.rationale: Epinephrine is first-line for anaphylaxis. Antihistamines do not replace epinephrine or emergency evaluation.

items.title: A client with chronic hypercapnic COPD is prescribed controlled oxygen. Which nursing actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.content: Use the prescribed delivery device and target saturation; reassess respiratory effort and mental status; obtain ABGs as ordered; titrate oxygen according to the prescribed plan.
items.rationale: Controlled oxygen reduces hypoxemia while avoiding unnecessary excess. Monitor clinical status and ABGs; never withhold oxygen from a hypoxemic client.

items.title: Select the 3 findings after myocardial infarction that require immediate escalation.
items.content: New hypotension; new pulmonary edema; sustained ventricular tachycardia.
items.rationale: These indicate cardiogenic shock, acute heart failure, or life-threatening dysrhythmia.

items.title: Match each medication with a serious adverse effect to report.
items.content: rows:ACE inhibitor;statin;amiodarone|columns:angioedema;unexplained muscle pain with dark urine;new dyspnea or cough|answers:ACE inhibitor=angioedema;statin=unexplained muscle pain with dark urine;amiodarone=new dyspnea or cough
items.rationale: ACE inhibitors can cause angioedema. Statins rarely cause rhabdomyolysis. Amiodarone can cause pulmonary toxicity.

items.title: A client with suspected STEMI should receive rapid ECG assessment and activation of the ___ pathway. The priority definitive treatment is timely ___ when indicated.
items.content: STEMI|reperfusion
items.rationale: STEMI requires rapid system activation and reperfusion, typically primary PCI when timely and appropriate.

items.title: A child sits leaning forward, drools, has a muffled voice, and inspiratory stridor. Select the condition, two actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:acute epiglottitis|actions:keep the child calm and avoid throat examination;activate expert airway support and prepare controlled airway management|monitor:work of breathing and oxygenation;level of consciousness
items.rationale: Epiglottitis can cause sudden airway obstruction. Avoid agitation and throat manipulation; secure expert airway support and monitor respiratory status.

items.title: Highlight findings in a client taking an antipsychotic that suggest neuroleptic malignant syndrome: high fever;severe muscle rigidity;altered mental status;lead-pipe rigidity;isolated mild rhinorrhea.
items.content: segments:high fever|severe muscle rigidity|altered mental status|lead-pipe rigidity|isolated mild rhinorrhea|correct:1,2,3,4
items.rationale: Hyperthermia, severe rigidity, and mental-status change after dopamine-blocking medication suggest neuroleptic malignant syndrome, a medical emergency.

items.title: A client's BP is 90/60 mm Hg. Calculate MAP using (SBP + 2 × DBP) ÷ 3. Enter a whole number.
items.content: 70|mm Hg|0

items.title: A postoperative client's temperature rises from 37.1 °C to 38.3 °C, HR from 88 to 116/min, and incision drainage becomes purulent. What is the priority?
items.content: Suspect surgical site infection with possible systemic involvement and notify the surgical team promptly.
items.rationale: Fever, tachycardia, and purulent drainage suggest infection requiring evaluation, cultures as ordered, and treatment.

items.title: A nurse discovers that a client received twice the prescribed dose of an antihypertensive 20 minutes ago. The client is currently asymptomatic. What should the nurse do?
items.content: Assess vital signs and symptoms immediately, notify the prescriber and appropriate safety personnel, follow orders for monitoring or treatment, and complete factual documentation and incident reporting per policy.
items.rationale: A medication error requires prompt assessment and disclosure through the appropriate clinical chain. Do not wait for symptoms or alter the record.

items.title: A client recovering from mild acute pancreatitis has improving pain and no vomiting. Which diet approach should the nurse anticipate?
items.content: Begin oral feeding as tolerated according to the prescribed plan, often with a low-fat approach.
items.rationale: Early oral feeding as tolerated is appropriate in many mild cases; prolonged routine NPO status is not necessary once symptoms permit intake.

items.title: Which findings suggest a client is ready for discharge after uncomplicated surgery? Select all that apply.
items.content: Stable vital signs; controlled pain with oral medication; tolerating oral fluids or diet as ordered; safe mobility at the expected level; unresolved new hypoxia.
items.rationale: Discharge requires stability and safe function. New hypoxia is a reason for further evaluation, not discharge.

items.title: Select the 3 findings that indicate worsening hepatic synthetic or neurologic function.
items.content: Rising INR; increasing confusion; recurrent hypoglycemia.
items.rationale: INR reflects impaired clotting factor synthesis; confusion suggests encephalopathy; hypoglycemia can occur with severe liver failure.

items.title: Match each wound drainage description with its term.
items.content: rows:clear watery drainage;pink-tinged thin drainage;thick yellow-green drainage|columns:serous;serosanguineous;purulent|answers:clear watery drainage=serous;pink-tinged thin drainage=serosanguineous;thick yellow-green drainage=purulent
items.rationale: Serous is clear, serosanguineous is pink-tinged, and purulent drainage is thick and may indicate infection.

items.title: Before thrombolytic therapy is considered for ischemic stroke, urgent brain imaging must exclude intracranial ___. The nurse must establish the last-known-___ time and check bedside ___.
items.content: hemorrhage|well|glucose
items.rationale: Imaging excludes hemorrhage, last-known-well time guides eligibility, and glucose identifies a common stroke mimic.

items.topic: Acute renal failure with fluid overload
items.title: A client with acute kidney injury has crackles, increasing edema, BP 182/100 mm Hg, and declining urine output. Select the condition, two actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:acute kidney injury with fluid overload|actions:notify the provider and prepare for prescribed fluid/diuretic or renal replacement plan;position to support breathing and restrict fluids only as prescribed|monitor:respiratory status and oxygenation;daily weight and intake/output
items.rationale: Oliguria with edema and crackles indicates fluid overload. Escalate, support breathing, and follow individualized fluid and renal treatment orders.

items.title: Highlight findings that suggest late neurovascular compromise: paralysis; pulselessness; pallor; severe pain; paresthesia.
items.content: segments:paralysis|pulselessness|pallor|severe pain|paresthesia|correct:1,2,3,4,5
items.rationale: All listed findings are concerning. Paralysis and pulselessness are late signs; intervention should occur before these develop.

items.title: A 500-mL IV bag is prescribed over 4 hours. What pump rate in mL/hr is required?
items.rationale: 500 mL ÷ 4 hr = 125 mL/hr.

items.title: A client with COPD has RR 28/min and SpO₂ 90% on prescribed oxygen. Later, RR falls to 10/min, the client becomes drowsy, and PaCO₂ rises. What does this trend indicate?
items.content: Worsening ventilatory failure and fatigue, requiring immediate escalation.
items.rationale: A falling respiratory rate with drowsiness and rising CO₂ may indicate fatigue rather than improvement.

items.title: A client at 36 weeks with preeclampsia has a generalized seizure. What are the immediate nursing priorities?
items.content: Call for help, protect the client from injury, position laterally when possible, support airway and oxygenation, administer prescribed magnesium sulfate, and prepare for maternal-fetal reassessment and delivery planning.
items.rationale: Eclampsia is an obstetric emergency. Stabilize airway and circulation, prevent injury, treat seizures with magnesium, and reassess mother and fetus.

items.title: A child with croup has stridor only when crying and no retractions at rest. Which intervention is most appropriate?
items.content: Keep the child calm and administer prescribed corticosteroid therapy.
items.rationale: Mild croup is managed with calm supportive care and corticosteroid treatment; agitation can worsen airway symptoms.

items.title: Which teaching points are appropriate for a client newly prescribed an oral anticoagulant for atrial fibrillation? Select all that apply.
items.content: Take the medication exactly as prescribed; report bleeding; inform clinicians before procedures; avoid starting OTC NSAIDs without advice.
items.rationale: Anticoagulation reduces embolic stroke risk but increases bleeding risk. Adherence and interaction awareness are essential.

items.title: Select the 3 findings that should trigger rapid response activation in a hospitalized adult.
items.content: Acute change in consciousness; severe respiratory distress; persistent hypotension with signs of poor perfusion.
items.rationale: These are indicators of potentially life-threatening deterioration requiring immediate escalation.

items.title: Match each breath sound with its common association.
items.content: rows:crackles;high-pitched wheeze;stridor|columns:fluid in alveoli or small airways;airflow through narrowed lower airways;upper airway obstruction|answers:crackles=fluid in alveoli or small airways;high-pitched wheeze=airflow through narrowed lower airways;stridor=upper airway obstruction
items.rationale: Crackles may reflect fluid or alveolar reopening, wheezes indicate narrowed lower airways, and stridor suggests upper airway obstruction.

items.title: A restraint may be used only after less restrictive measures fail and with an appropriate ___ and ongoing ___ according to policy. The client must be released as soon as it is ___ to do so.
items.content: order|monitoring|safe
items.rationale: Restraints require legal and policy-compliant authorization, ongoing reassessment, and prompt discontinuation when no longer necessary.

items.title: A septic client develops oozing from IV sites, petechiae, platelets 42,000/mm³, and prolonged PT/aPTT. Select the condition, two actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:disseminated intravascular coagulation|actions:notify the critical care team and treat the underlying sepsis;implement bleeding precautions and prepare prescribed blood component support|monitor:platelet count and coagulation studies;clinical bleeding and organ perfusion
items.rationale: DIC causes consumption of platelets and clotting factors with simultaneous bleeding and thrombosis. Treat the cause, support coagulation as prescribed, and monitor bleeding and perfusion.

items.title: Highlight findings of acute pulmonary edema: pink frothy sputum;severe dyspnea;bilateral crackles;orthopnea;dry cough without hypoxia or distress.
items.content: segments:pink frothy sputum|severe dyspnea|bilateral crackles|orthopnea|dry cough without hypoxia or distress|correct:1,2,3,4
items.rationale: Pink frothy sputum, severe dyspnea, crackles, and orthopnea are consistent with pulmonary edema.

items.title: A child weighs 20 kg. Using the 4-2-1 rule, calculate the hourly maintenance fluid rate in mL/hr.
items.content: 60|mL/hr|0
items.rationale: For the first 10 kg: 4 mL/kg/hr = 40; next 10 kg: 2 mL/kg/hr = 20; total 60 mL/hr. Clinical orders may use different methods and require reassessment.

items.title: A client with chest pain has troponin values that rise from 18 to 240 ng/L over 3 hours and develops new ST depression. What is the priority interpretation?
items.content: Evolving myocardial injury with ongoing ischemia; escalate urgently for acute coronary syndrome management.
items.rationale: A rising troponin with ischemic ECG changes supports acute myocardial injury and requires urgent evaluation and treatment.

items.title: A 24-year-old with asthma has severe dyspnea, speaks in short phrases, RR 32/min, and SpO₂ 88%. After repeated rescue treatment, the client becomes drowsy and wheezing is no longer audible. What should the nurse do?
items.content: Activate emergency airway support immediately; provide oxygen and prescribed rescue therapy while preparing for ventilatory support.
items.rationale: Loss of wheezing with drowsiness in a severely distressed client may indicate minimal airflow and impending respiratory arrest, not recovery.

items.title: A client says they take an herbal supplement but cannot recall its name. What should the nurse do?
items.content: Ask the client to bring the container or obtain the exact product and dose before evaluating interactions.
items.rationale: Herbal products can interact with prescribed medications; identify the exact product, dose, and frequency rather than assuming its contents.

items.title: A client with a new ileostomy has output of 2.2 L/day and dizziness. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.content: Assess vital signs and orthostatic symptoms; monitor electrolytes and renal function; notify the care team; follow prescribed oral rehydration and output management plan.
items.rationale: High ileostomy output can cause dehydration, electrolyte loss, and acute kidney injury. Prompt assessment and individualized replacement are needed.

items.title: Select the 3 findings that support suspected aortic dissection.
items.content: Abrupt tearing chest or back pain; unequal peripheral pulses or arm blood pressures; new neurologic deficit or syncope.
items.rationale: Abrupt tearing pain with pulse/BP differential or neurologic symptoms is concerning for dissection and requires emergency evaluation.

items.title: For each sick-day instruction, select whether it is appropriate.
items.content: rows:continue basal insulin unless specifically directed otherwise;check glucose more frequently;check ketones when indicated;stop all fluids during vomiting|columns:appropriate;inappropriate|answers:continue basal insulin unless specifically directed otherwise=appropriate;check glucose more frequently=appropriate;check ketones when indicated=appropriate;stop all fluids during vomiting=inappropriate
items.rationale: Sick-day plans generally continue basal insulin, increase glucose monitoring, check ketones when indicated, and maintain hydration with urgent care for red flags.

items.title: Arrange the immediate sequence for a client with suspected acute stroke.
items.content: Activate stroke response and record last-known-well time.|Assess ABCs and check bedside glucose.|Prepare for urgent noncontrast head CT.|Maintain NPO status until swallow screening is completed.
items.rationale: Rapid activation and time documentation are followed by stabilization and glucose assessment, imaging, and aspiration precautions.

items.title: Select all appropriate actions before administering a high-alert medication.
items.content: Verify the prescription and patient identity; check relevant laboratory results; use the required independent double-check per policy; program the infusion pump using the approved protocol; bypass barcode scanning if the unit is busy.
items.rationale: High-alert medications require verification, relevant monitoring, and policy-based safeguards. Workflow pressure is not a reason to bypass safety checks.

items.title: A client with a known neck mass develops stridor, drooling, and inability to speak full sentences. SpO₂ is 90%. What is the priority response?
items.content: Activate emergency airway support, keep the client upright and calm, provide oxygen as tolerated, and prepare for controlled airway management. Avoid unnecessary oral or throat manipulation.
items.rationale: Stridor and drooling suggest critical upper airway narrowing. Early expert airway management is safer than waiting for complete obstruction.

items.title: A newborn is wet immediately after birth. Which action best prevents heat loss?
items.content: Dry the newborn thoroughly and remove wet linens.
items.rationale: Evaporation from wet skin causes neonatal heat loss. Drying and replacing wet linens are immediate measures.

items.title: Which actions reduce medication errors in children? Select all that apply.
items.content: Use current weight in kilograms; calculate dose by weight and verify maximum dose; use an oral syringe for liquid medication; perform an independent check when required.
items.rationale: Pediatric dosing is weight-based and errors can be serious. Use kilograms, verify maximums, and measure liquids accurately.

items.title: A client in alcohol withdrawal has a generalized seizure. Select the 3 priority actions.
items.content: Protect the client from injury; maintain airway and position laterally when possible; administer prescribed benzodiazepine and activate urgent support.
items.rationale: Seizure safety, airway protection, and benzodiazepine treatment are priorities in alcohol withdrawal.

items.title: Match each presentation with the likely acute complication.
items.content: rows:deep rapid breathing, abdominal pain, ketones;profound dehydration, very high glucose, high osmolality;confusion and sweating with glucose 42 mg/dL|columns:diabetic ketoacidosis;hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state;hypoglycemia|answers:deep rapid breathing, abdominal pain, ketones=diabetic ketoacidosis;profound dehydration, very high glucose, high osmolality=hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state;confusion and sweating with glucose 42 mg/dL=hypoglycemia
items.rationale: DKA includes ketosis and metabolic acidosis. HHS features severe hyperglycemia and hyperosmolality. Low glucose with autonomic/neuroglycopenic symptoms indicates hypoglycemia.
